data.name: Imtiyaz
data.gender_notes: Imtiyaz is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Imtiyaz means 'distinction' or 'honor' in Arabic. This name is derived from the word 'imtidad' which means 'to honor'. The name Imtiyaz carries the meaning “Distinction, Honor” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Imtiyaz usually hope their child will grow to embody distinction, honor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Islamic tradition, Imtiyaz is considered a noble name as it signifies respect and admiration. It is often given to children who are expected to excel in their fields and bring pride to their families.
data.etymology: Imtiyaz belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Distinction, Honor.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Imtiyaz total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: امتیاز
in_arabic.meaning: فضل و کرم سے ممتاز ہونا، اللہ کی خاص رحمت

in_urdu.name: امتیاز
in_urdu.meaning: فضل و کرم سے ممتاز ہونا، اللہ کی خاص رحمت
in_urdu.long_meaning: امتیاز ایک ایسا نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے اور فضل و کرم سے ممتاز ہونے کی خصوصیت رکھتا ہے۔ یہ اللہ کی خاص رحمت اور مہربانی کا اظہار کرتا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کے ثقافت میں یہ نام بہت اہمیت رکھتا ہے اور اکثر ایسے بچوں کے لیے منتخب کیا جاتا ہے جن کے والدین چاہتے ہیں کہ ان کے بچے اللہ کی رحمت اور فضل سے نوازے جائیں۔

in_hindi.name: इम्तियाज़

in_english.name: Imtiyaz
in_english.meaning: distinguished by special favor or grace
in_english.long_meaning: Imtiyaz is a name derived from Arabic roots, signifying 'distinguished by special favor or grace.' It originates from the Arabic root 'm-t-y-z,' meaning 'to distinguish' or 'to bestow favor.' While not directly mentioned in the Quran, the concept is aligned with Islamic values of divine grace and mercy. Historically, the name has been used across various Muslim cultures, reflecting the spiritual significance of being favored by Allah. It symbolizes the hope that the bearer will be endowed with divine blessings and mercy.
